name: Light Perilla Purple
lede: Light Perilla Purple is a paler reading of [[perilla-purple|Perilla Purple]], the dusty reddish mauve Robert Ridgway named for the East Asian herb perilla in his 1912 color atlas.

sections.title: A modifier on a leaf color
sections.body:
The name is built by grammar: "light" over the parent [[perilla-purple|Perilla Purple]], itself named for the dark purple-red leaves of perilla, the herb better known in the kitchen as shiso [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plates this lighter step on plate XXXVII, hue 65'', tone i [1]. Measured, it reads lighter than its parent (lightness 48 against 38) at a close chroma, keeping the same muted, reddish cast [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[mauve-taupe|Mauve-Taupe]], 3.9 units away and redder, with [[daphne-red|Daphne Red]] close behind at 4.1, more vivid [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this dusty mauve in 15 of 23,781 paintings (0.06 percent, as photographed), rarer than 82 percent of the named colors we track [2]. The earliest dated match runs to 1780, by Joseph-Siffred Duplessis, 132 years before Ridgway's 1912 record; the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof the pigment was there, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
